# Load & Stress Test Report — AdonERP

**Date:** 2026-11-10

> **Environment caveat:** no isolated staging environment was available. Tests ran against a **local production build** (`next start -p 3100`, single Node process) on the developer's Windows machine with the local Postgres database. Results show relative capacity and bottlenecks, **not** production capacity. Production was not touched.

**Tool:** `autocannon@8.0.0`, 20 s per step, stepped concurrency 10 → 50 → 100.
**Data:** existing local data (12 blog posts, pricing content). No writes were generated by the load test (GET only).

## Results

### Page render — `GET /en/pricing`

| Concurrency | Req/s (avg) | p50 | p90 | p99 | max | Errors / non-2xx / timeouts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 16 | 635 ms | 746 ms | 915 ms | 958 ms | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| 50 | 15 | 3,184 ms | 3,462 ms | 3,713 ms | 3,713 ms | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| 100 | 13 | 6,595 ms | 7,140 ms | 7,531 ms | 7,532 ms | 0 / 0 / 0 |

**Interpretation:** throughput is flat at ~15 req/s — the process is CPU-saturated from the first step; extra concurrency only queues. Each request costs ~65 ms of server CPU (dynamic SSR + serialising a ~1.1 MB RSC payload). No errors or crashes under 100 concurrent connections: the failure mode is latency, not instability.

### API — `GET /api/blog?limit=9` (Prisma → Postgres)

| Concurrency | Req/s (avg) | p50 | p99 | Errors / non-2xx |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 567 → **608** after pool change | 15–16 ms | 23–24 ms | 0 / 0 |
| 50 | 669 | 73 ms | 100 ms | 0 / 0 |
| 100 | 670 → **637** after pool change | 146–154 ms | 203–204 ms | 0 / 0 |

The database path is healthy and ~40× faster than page rendering. Capping the pool at 5 connections (CODE_AUDIT F2) did not reduce throughput meaningfully.

### Rate-limit behaviour under burst (functional, from security suite)
- `POST /api/analytics/collect`: requests 1–120 from one IP → 200, 121+ → 429; another IP unaffected.

### Full-site crawl (8 concurrent, 2,952 URLs)
All 200, p50 682 ms, p99 990 ms, max 2.6 s. No errors.

## Bottleneck & capacity estimate
- **Single process:** ~15 page views/s ≈ 54,000/hour sustained, with latency degrading sharply above ~10 concurrent requests.
- **Main levers** (see PERFORMANCE_REPORT P1/P2): static rendering/ISR + CDN removes per-request SSR entirely; trimming the message payload cuts per-request CPU even while dynamic.

## Resource usage
Not instrumented (no APM/metrics agent locally). CPU saturation is inferred from flat throughput with rising latency.

## Not performed
- Staging-environment load test with production-like hardware, network and data volume.
- Soak test (multi-hour) for memory leaks.
- Write-path load (demo requests, analytics ingestion at volume) — would insert data; requires staging DB.
- Spike test beyond 100 connections.

## Recommended next actions
1. Before launch, repeat these steps on staging using the same commands:
   `npx autocannon@8.0.0 -c 10|50|100 -d 60 https://<staging>/en/pricing`
2. If self-hosting: run ≥ one Node process per CPU core (PM2 cluster / multiple containers) and put a CDN in front.
3. After P1/P2, re-run; expect page throughput to be bounded by the CDN instead of Node.
